notes.claim: A multiplication table extended to negative numbers shows, by following its pattern, the effect of multiplying by a negative number.
Multiplying two numbers with the same sign gives a positive answer, so (−3) × (−2) = +6, and multiplying two numbers with different signs gives a negative answer.
Students can lose sight of the fact that the sign rule is for multiplying, not adding, and some apply it when adding or subtracting.

sources.title: Sources and Possible Causes of Errors and Misconceptions in Operations of Integers — International Electronic Journal of Mathematics Education (ERIC)
sources.quote: Some apply this rule when adding or subtracting integers although this rule is used when multiplying or dividing numbers.

sources.title: Sources and Possible Causes of Errors and Misconceptions in Operations of Integers — International Electronic Journal of Mathematics Education (ERIC)
sources.quote: The fact that the rules are only applied to the multiplication of a positive and a negative integer and not for the addition of integers is lost without proper understanding.

sources.title: How to multiply and divide positive and negative numbers – KS3 Maths – BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: This multiplication table includes both positive and negative numbers. Follow the pattern to see the effect of multiplying by negative numbers.

sources.title: How to multiply and divide positive and negative numbers – KS3 Maths – BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Calculate 3 × 2 initially to get 6, then remember that multiplying two numbers with the same sign means the answer will be positive, (-3) × (-2) = +6
